reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend and adds isHoliday, but each consumer writes its own 'daily and skipWeekend and (weekend or holiday)' skip instead of a shared occurrence-adjustment function, and schedule-template.ts is not given holidays.

duplication.why: The daily skip predicate appears four times (two find closures in getNextDate, a filter in getUpcomingDates, a map-to-null in getDatesInRange), and the 'skipWeekend ? getDateWithSkippedWeekend(...) : date' adjustment is repeated in every consumer.

placement.why: The weekend/holiday move lives in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily-skip rule is spread between shared/schedules.ts and server/schedules/app.ts instead of one shared definition.

scope.why: The edits serve the four requests, with a type field and tests; no unrelated changes.

maintainability.why: Weekend/holiday semantics now differ by call site (holidays read from dateCond.value in one place, schedule.data in another; template path ignores holidays), so a future rule change has to find five places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange re-implement the daily skip around getDateWithSkippedWeekend; server/budget/schedule-template.ts still calls getDateWithSkippedWeekend without holidays or the daily skip

disguised_duplication.where: the daily weekend/holiday skip is written as a find predicate twice in getNextDate, a .filter in getUpcomingDates and a map-to-null in getDatesInRange

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains skipDailyWeekends branches (forward lookup and reverse fallback) and excludes the shared weekend move for daily; getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange re-implement the daily skip; schedule-template.ts calls the helper without holidays
